Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

surprise verb

catch unawares

also take by surprise, catch off guard, by surprise, unexpectedly

classical

Hirt. B.G. 8.36.3: dē imprōvīsō (Lewis & Short, s.v. imprūdēns)
Erasm. Coll., Fōrm.

dē imprōvīsō opprimō, opprimere, oppressī, oppressum

come on someone unexpectedly, take by surprise

Opprimere is “to fall on, overwhelm”; with dē imprōvīsō or ex imprōvīsō (“unexpectedly”) it is to catch someone off guard. To surprise someone with a present is dē imprōvīsō dōnāre.

Other words

  • imprūdentem opprimō — catch someone unawares

    also used · classical · Ter. And. 226–227 (M-O s.v. surprise vb)

    Morgan–Owens’ phrase, from Terence: the person caught is imprūdēns, “not expecting it”.

  • dēprehendō, dēprehendere, dēprehendī, dēprehēnsum — catch (in the act)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. dēprehendō

    Catching someone doing something, found out.

Examples

  • Dē imprōvīsō tē opprimam. … Tē nec opīnantem oppresserō.

    I’ll take you by surprise. … I’ll pounce on you when you least expect it.Erasm. Coll., Fōrmulae, Invītandī ad convīvium

  • nē dē hāc rē pater inprūdentem opprimat

    so that my father doesn’t catch him unawares with this businessTer. And. 226–227 (M-O s.v. surprise vb)

See also be surprised, surprise, amaze, suddenly.
